WHY COURAGE, CONVICTION AND CLARITY ARE NEEDED NOW MORE THAN EVER

I’ve been in the Philippines all week. Yesterday, as I talked to a chaplain for a large Christian school here, I was surprised to discover how deeply the teens and teachers he ministered to were impacted by the news of Charlie Kirk’s death.

All this week I’ve been spending time with 200 youth movement leaders from 70 countries who gathered in Manila to collaborate. After we heard the news of Charlie Kirk’s horrifying assassination, I realized how far reaching his impact was/is on Gen Z, not just across the United States, but around the world. 

@colmflynnire, in an article in today’s @nypost, shared some insights about why so many young people globally resonated with his message and approach, “We live in a time of uncertainty and change, as AI technology raises existential questions about jobs and humanity, wars rage across the globe, and even matters of basic biology spark fierce debate. Amid this chaos, confusion reigns, and our youth crave clarity, stability and above all, meaning.”

Speaking specifically of @charliekirk11 he goes on to write, “But his call to live a Christian life echoed far beyond borders, touching millions of young hearts — and his Christian witness cut deeper than his fiery political rhetoric. His unapologetic defense of faith, his example as a devoted father and family man, and his proud upholding of Christian values empowered young men, in particular, to speak openly about aspiring to families and virtuous lives — ideals sidelined in a culture obsessed with fame, fortune and followers.”

In a world of relentless confusion, never-ending scrolling and deeply imbedded anxiety, young people are looking for courage, conviction and clarity.

Charlie had all three of these in abundance, which brings me to my point.

May we choose to live and lead with courage, conviction and clarity. May we be unafraid to speak the Gospel passionately and persuasively in a world of young people who are desperate for a solid foundation to build their lives upon.

This is what the great apostle, who lost his head at the hands of a Nero-appointed executioner, reminded a younger timid Timothy in his last letter before his death,

“For the Spirit God gave us does not make us timid, but gives us power, love and self-discipline. So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of me his prisoner. Rather, join with me in suffering for the gospel, by the power of God.” 2 Timothy 1:7,8

May we be willing to suffer for the Gospel by the power of God.

May we mobilize our believing teenagers worldwide to harness this level of heroic boldness to speak out and live out the Gospel, not necessarily from a pop-up tent in the middle of a university, but in every single conversation with their peers both face-to-face and online.

There is one more “c” I would add to the list of courage, conviction and clarity and that is compassion.

At times like this, when the world is inflamed, for or against whatever, there is a temptation to enter the fray with anger and bitterness.

But we must remember the example we follow is Jesus Christ. He was the perfect balance of courage, conviction, clarity and compassion.

“When he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.” Matthew 9:36

The Greek word for “compassion” is “splagchnizomai.” It means to have your very guts yearn in compassion for others in pain. Our hearts must be broken for those we are seeking to reach, because when the fire of conviction mixes with the tears of compassion the Gospel we preach becomes an irresistible force.

So let us courageously go forward from this tragic week. Let us share the Gospel truth with clarity and conviction. Let us do it with Jesus-level compassion for those we are speaking to.

Let us equip our young people to do the same.

Here’s a simple way to get them started: https://t.co/dUAVviYpmF
